games.overallPlan: Against Spielmann's central gambit in the Bishop's Opening, Black declines greedy pawn-grabbing with 6...d3 to return the pawn and hold back White's development, then exploits White's overextended queenside and kingside pawns with a central passed e-pawn and 25...Nf4!.

annotations.summary: Capturing 4...Nxe4 allows 5. Qxd4 with a dangerous initiative for a single pawn; Alekhine avoids material gain that costs development time.

variations.summary: Grants White a fierce lead in development.

annotations.summary: If White advances 5. e5 immediately, Black strikes the centre with 5...d5.

variations.summary: Black counterattacks the bishop and centre immediately.

annotations.summary: Giving back the gambit pawn prevents White from accelerating development via 6...dxc3 7. Nxc3 and 8. Bg5.

variations.summary: Leaves White with effortless open lines and rapid development.

annotations.summary: Though 8. b4 weakens the queenside, White avoids quiet symmetry like 9. Bg5 h6 10. Bh4 Bg4 11. Nbd2 Ne5 where Black equalizes effortlessly.

variations.summary: Quiet play gives Black comfortable equality.

annotations.summary: Forces accurate play against Black's uncastled king and prevents ...Nxc4 followed by easy castling.
Crucial parry to the threat of 14. Ba3, compelling White to abandon direct attack and catch up on development.
Threatens to win material with 15...Bd6.
Provokes 18. f4, permanently denying White a later central break with f3.
Defends e4 against 20...Bxe5 21. fxe5 Bxc4 22. Rxe4; moving the other rook (20. Rae1) fails to 20...Bxe5 21. fxe5 Bxb3.

variations.summary: White keeps material balance if the f1-rook occupies e1.

annotations.summary: Establishes an awkward passed pawn while highlighting the holes created by White's early flank advances.
Eliminating the passed pawn with 21. Kg2 was marginally better, yet 21...Bxe5 22. fxe5 Bxc4 23. Rxe3 Kf7 24. exf6 gxf6 still leaves a favourable endgame for Black.

variations.summary: Endgame remains clearly better for Black.

annotations.summary: Passively defending the pawn leaves Black overwhelming pressure after ...Nxf4 and ...Rxf4; White chooses a desperate piece sacrifice instead.
annotations.note: Book annotation writes 23. B x P, 23...Kt x K B P, 24. B x Kt, R x B, but White's c1/g5 bishop cannot capture on e3 through White's f4 pawn; 23. Rxe3 Nxe3+ or 23. Rxe3 Nxf4 is likely intended.

annotations.summary: The only winning continuation: both 25...Rf3 26. Bg6+ and 25...Ne7 26. Rad1 Bxe1 27. Rd7 Bb4 28. Bxe7 would let White escape with dangerous counterplay.

variations.summary: Gives White active compensation.
White's bishops generate decisive counter-threats.

annotations.summary: Avoids the final swindle 27...Ne2+ 28. Kg2 Rf2+ 29. Kh1 Bb4 30. Rxg7 where White threatens mate and forces a perpetual check.

variations.summary: Swindle leading only to perpetual check.

errata.note: Annotation to 23. f5 prints '23. B x P, Kt x K B P; 24. B x Kt, R x B' on p. 30; neither White bishop can capture on e3 because White's pawn occupies f4 (23. Rxe3 would fail to 23...Nxf4 24. Bxf4 Rxf4 or 23...Nxe3+).

games.chapterTitle: All-Russian Masters' Tournament at Vilna, September, 1912
games.overallPlan: Black avoids premature queenside weakening after fianchettoing, secures d5 via 16...f5!, and meets White's misguided 21. Bg5 with a combinational Exchange-and-pawn counterstroke featuring 21...Nxc3 22. Bxg6 Qd5 and a decisive endgame victory capped by 36...Rd2!.

annotations.summary: Critiques Schlechter's fianchetto in this Slav pawn structure because g7 has limited scope; notes that after 4. Nc3 dxc4 5. e3 b5 or 5. a4 Bf5! Black achieves counterplay.
Keeps the queenside intact rather than releasing tension with 8...dxc4 followed by ...b5 and ...b4 as in Lasker–Schlechter (1910).
Recapturing with the knight avoids giving White control of the open c-file after 10...cxd5.

variations.summary: If White delays cxd5, both QBP pawns are exchanged and Black activates comfortably with ...c5 and ...Na6.

annotations.summary: If White instead strikes in the centre with 14. e4, Black answers 14...cxd4 15. cxd4 Qd6 with good play.

variations.summary: Central expansion gives Black easy targets.

subvariations.summary: Also yields Black a sound position.

annotations.summary: Prevents 16. Qa4! which would follow 15...f5.

variations.summary: White hits the weakened queenside immediately.

annotations.summary: Fixes permanent control over the d5 outpost after White omitted the essential 16. e4.

variations.summary: Keeps balanced chances instead of retreating the knight to d2.

annotations.summary: Refutes 21. Bg5 tactically: 22. Bxa8 Nxb1 leaves Black an Exchange ahead.

variations.summary: Black wins the Exchange outright and stays attacking.

annotations.summary: Superior to grabbing 22...Nxb1 immediately, as 23. Bxh7+ Kh8 24. Qg6 Qe8 25. Qxc2 would yield White dangerous dark-squared compensation.

variations.summary: White achieves strong attacking compensation for the Exchange.

annotations.summary: Forces the queen exchange since 27. Kh2 allows 27...Rxf4! 28. Bxf4 Qxf4+.

variations.summary: Black wins cleanly against a passive king retreat.

annotations.summary: Seeking kingside counterplay with 30. Bh6 achieves nothing against 30...Rg8 31. g4 a5.

variations.summary: Black halts White's kingside pawns easily.

annotations.summary: If White instead captures 32. Nxc4, 32...Rc6 33. Ne3 Rc3 34. Re1 Rxa3 wins cleanly; Alekhine abandons the h-checks to contest the d-file.

variations.summary: Decisive simplification for Black.

annotations.summary: Parries the mating threat and traps the c2 bishop with no flight square.

games.chapterTitle: All-Russian Masters' Tournament at Vilna, September, 1912
games.overallPlan: Against Nimzowitsch's early queenside and kingside pawn pushes, Alekhine sidesteps White's 15. O-O-O trap with 15...Bd6!, then breaks open the queenside with 17...c4! and 20...Rb6! to hunt down and trap White's overextended queen.

annotations.summary: Better options were 7...Bxf3 or 7...cxd4, whereas keeping the bishop allows White to expand simultaneously on both wings.

variations.summary: Sound queenside and central structure.
Active counterplay for Black.

annotations.summary: Spots and sidesteps White's tactical trap: 15...cxd4 16. exd4 Nxd4 17. Rxd4 Qxd4 18. Qxe6+ Nd7 19. Qc6+! bxc6 20. Ba6#.

variations.summary: The hidden mating trap set by 15. O-O-O.

annotations.summary: Better was 17. Bxc6 bxc6 18. Rhg1 Rd7; the text allows 17...c4!.

variations.summary: Preferable defensive setup, though Black retains an edge.

annotations.summary: Drives back White's bishop and starts a coordinated offensive on both wings.
Sets a tactical counter-threat of a queen-sacrifice mate via ...Qxb2, ...Qxc3+ and ...Ne4#.
annotations.note: Book annotation writes 21...Kt x B; 22. R x Kt, Q x Kt P; 23. R—Q Kt 1, Q x Kt ch; 24. K x Q, Kt—K 5 mate, although neither black knight reaches g6; the immediate 21...Qxb2! carries the same mate threat.

variations.summary: Mating idea if White ignores the threat to b2.

annotations.summary: White sacrifices a piece desperately seeking queen counterplay; 24. Bg6? loses outright to 24...Nxh4! threatening ...Ne4+ if White captures the knight.

variations.summary: Decisive royal fork winning the queen.

annotations.summary: White's queen has no escape: 37. Rxg6 Nxg6 38. Rxg7+ Kc6 39. Qxb7 Rxh4 leaves White defenseless.

games.chapterTitle: All-Russian Masters' Tournament at Vilna, September, 1912
games.overallPlan: White turns Black's miscoordinated queenside manoeuvres against the Paulsen Sicilian with 18. e5! and 22. a4!, winning the Exchange when Black cuts off his own queen's retreat before finishing with a doubled-rook invasion on the 7th rank.

annotations.summary: Notes retrospectively that 3. Be2 is preferable to preserve the option of advancing c4 against a Paulsen setup.
Unexpected thrust that captures the initiative: advancing 18...d5 allows 19. Bxd5! exd5 20. Nxd5 Qd8 21. Bc5 with crushing pressure.

variations.summary: Black's queenside collapses if he ignores the bishop on d5.
Black's queenside collapses after 19...exd5 as well.

annotations.summary: Punishes 21...Na8, which removed the queen's retreat square: 22...Bxc5 23. Bxc5 Rfc8 24. c3 Bxa4 25. Bd1 bxc3 26. b4 wins decisively.

variations.summary: White wins cleanly against 22...Bxc5.

annotations.summary: Precision move threatening 36. Rxg7+ Nxg7 37. Qf7+ Kh8 38. Qf8+ Rxf8 39. Rxf8#, avoiding the premature 35. Rxg7+ Kxg7 which only draws.

variations.summary: Mate pattern created by 35. Qa7.

annotations.summary: Stops Black's counter-threats cleanly while a6–a7 promotes; White's rook and queen dominate.
annotations.note: Book scores 46. Q—Kt 1 without K/Q prefix; 46. Qb1 is blocked by Black's queen on c1, so 46. Qg1 (Q—K Kt 1) is the unique legal queen move to the first rank's knight file.

errata.note: Move 46 on p. 40 is printed as '46. Q—Kt 1'; with Black's queen on c1 blocking f1–b1, only 46. Qg1 ('Q—K Kt 1') is legal.

games.chapterTitle: All-Russian Masters' Tournament at Vilna, September, 1912
games.overallPlan: Once White locks the centre with 12. d4 and weakens h3, Alekhine closes it completely after 12...f6! and 13...g5!, mounts a massive kingside pawn storm, shifts his queen and bishop across the a7–g1 diagonal, and concludes with 34...Nxf5! and a forced mate in five.

annotations.summary: Illustrates Alekhine's strategic principle: stabilize the centre before advancing pawns on either wing.
The logical thematic reaction against 7. h3, threatening ...g4 to rip open the g-file and compelling 14. d5.
Breaks open White's kingside at the decisive moment; capturing 35. Qxb2 fails to 35...Nh4+ 36. Kh1 Qd3.

variations.summary: Crushing tactical win if White takes the bishop.

annotations.summary: Announces forced mate in five; retreating 39. Kf1 allows 39...Qg1+ 40. Ke2 Qe3+ 41. Kd1 Qxe1#.

variations.summary: Also wins quickly on the back rank.

games.chapterTitle: Masters' Quadrangular Tournament at St. Petersburg, April, 1913
games.overallPlan: After gaining the open a-file with 7. a4!, White punishes Black's premature 13...Nd4 exchange by breaking in the centre with 16. e5! and orchestrating a knight sacrifice on f7 after the sneaky preparatory push 22. g4!.

annotations.summary: Opens the a-file with decisive effect; Black cannot close it with 7...b4 because 8. Bxf7+ Kxf7 9. Qc4+ d5 10. Qxc5 Qd6 11. Qxc6! wins.

variations.summary: Tactical refutation of 7...b4.

annotations.summary: Launches the decisive offensive against f7, fully exploiting the open a-file alongside both alternative Black defences 16...dxe5 and 16...Rfe8.

variations.summary: Clean positional advantage in the endgame.
Sharp refutation of 16...Rfe8.

subvariations.summary: Even stronger for White if the king flees to the corner.

annotations.summary: Subtle preparation for the f7 knight sacrifice; playing 22. Qf5 right away allowed Black to defend via 22...g6 followed by ...Kg7.

variations.summary: After 21...Nd7 White strikes on f7 immediately.

annotations.summary: Sets up twin threats of 25. Bxf7+ followed by 26. g5 and 25. Qe6, leaving Black defenseless.

games.chapterTitle: Masters' Quadrangular Tournament at St. Petersburg, April, 1913
games.overallPlan: Facing a premature kingside pawn storm with 12. g4 and 13. h4, Alekhine counterattacks first on the queenside via 15...Qb8! and 17...Rfd8!, repairs his doubled c-pawn, creates a dominating passed d-pawn, and breaks open the king with 33...c4!.

annotations.summary: Notes that 5. Bd2 is stronger than 5. d4, and cites Réti–Spielmann (Berlin 1920) where 6. d5 b5 7. dxc6 bxa4 8. c4! favours White.

variations.summary: White's queenside bind from Réti–Spielmann 1920.

annotations.summary: Stronger than grabbing 17...Qc3 immediately, which lets White contest the c-file and equalize via 18. Kf2 Qxc2 19. Rhc1 Qb2 20. Nc4! Qxe2+ 21. Kxe2.

variations.summary: Allows White easy positional compensation for the pawn.

annotations.summary: A temporary pawn sacrifice forcing Black's heavy pieces into White's camp while the passed c-pawn paralyses the defenders.
Forces open the h-file and decides at once against White's exposed king; 43...cxb2 would give White defensive chances via 44. Qe2!.

variations.summary: Mainline refutation if White captures en passant.

games.overallPlan: After White unwisely parts with the bishop pair on move 4 and advances h3, Alekhine closes the queenside via 10...b6! and 12...c5!, launches a kingside pawn storm, declines the Greek Gift 19. Bxc5 with 19...Bxf3 and 20...Rg8!, and breaks into the white king with 25...h5!.

annotations.summary: Surrendering the bishop pair does not challenge Bird's Defence; 4. Nxd4 exd4 5. O-O c6 6. Bc4 Ne7 7. d3 followed by c3 is theory's strongest reply.

variations.summary: Correct theoretical path against Bird's Defence.

annotations.summary: Prepares ...Ba6 while locking the centre if White tries to obstruct that diagonal before Black strikes on the kingside.
Calmly ignores White's piece sacrifice; 21. Be3 walks into 21...Rxg2+! 22. Kxg2 Qg4+ 23. Kh2 Qxf3 with a crushing kingside attack.

variations.summary: Demolishes White's kingside if he plays quietly.

annotations.summary: Denies White time for f3 and Rook lateral defence, maintaining a winning assault.
White's passed d7 pawn cannot save him; 30. Rd2 allows 30...Qh3 31. Rg2 Qxg2# and 30. Kf2 walks into 30...Rg6!.

variations.summary: Immediate back-rank mate.

games.overallPlan: Facing Mieses' early queen sortie in the Centre Game, Alekhine seizes central space with 7...d5!, carries out a deep positional queen sacrifice via 11...Nxc3! 12. Rxd8 Nxa2+ 13. Kb1 Rxd8 for Rook, Knight, Pawn and dominating pieces, and concludes with 27...Rb5! and 30...Rc8!.

annotations.summary: Notes 4...Nf6 was also good since 5. e5 Ng4 6. Qe4 d5! 7. exd6+ Be6 favours Black.

variations.summary: Aggressive gambit trap turns in Black's favour.

annotations.summary: Initiates the deep queen sacrifice; Alekhine later suggests 10...Nxc3 11. Bxc3 Qg5+ 12. Bd2 Qc5 13. Be3 Qa5 would have yielded a simpler positional edge.

variations.summary: Quiet positional alternative keeping Black clearly on top.

annotations.summary: Gets Rook, Knight and Pawn plus strong initiative for the Queen; much stronger than 11...Ndb4 12. a3 Ndxc3 13. Rxd8 Nba2+ 14. Kd2 Nb1+ 15. Ke1.

variations.summary: Black's knights end up stranded without coordination.

annotations.summary: Forces White to accept the knight, as 28. b3 Ra5 29. cxd3 cxb3 wins rapidly.

variations.summary: White is helpless against ...Ra1+ despite owning Queen for Rook.

annotations.summary: Even White's sole defence 31. Rg2 loses to 31...Rb1+ 32. Kd2 Rb3 33. Kd1 Bc3! 34. Bc1 Bb4!, confirming the complete soundness of the move-11 queen sacrifice.

variations.summary: Refutes the critics' suggested 31. Rg2.

subvariations.summary: Wins immediately on the back rank.

games.chapterTitle: All-Russian Masters' Tournament at St. Petersburg, January, 1914
games.overallPlan: Alekhine snaps up the e5 pawn with 10. Ng5! after 9...dxe4, relentlessly pressures the e5 blockader to turn his passed a-pawn into a monster at a7, sacrifices on b3 with 20. b3! to castle safely, and breaks Black's queenside blockade with 22. Qc5!.

annotations.summary: Notes 8. d4! was stronger (not 8. d5 because of 8...Bd6!), e.g. 8...d6 9. d5 Na5 10. Bc2 followed by Nbd2 and a4.
Tempting capture (QPxP in descriptive notation) that drops into tactical complications; 9...Bg4! 10. d3! secured equality at least.

variations.summary: Equalizes comfortably for Black.

annotations.summary: Wins a pawn safely because 10...Bg4 meets 11. Nxf7! Rxf7 12. Qc4!, winning at least the Exchange.

variations.summary: Refs the tempting pin 10...Bg4.

annotations.summary: Sacrifices a pawn to break Black's pin/bind and castle cleanly, unleashing the passed a7 pawn.
Decisive: taking the rook (22. Bxa8) allows 22...Nxe3 23. Bd5 Nxd5 24. a8=Q Nxc3 25. dxc3 Qxc3 with too much compensation; the text threatens 23. Bxa8 followed by Qc6.

variations.summary: Gives Black dangerous bishop-pair and pawn compensation.
Wins on the spot after 22. Qc5!.
